- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.16) and model forecast is high, reduce forecast by 1-2% to avoid overreaction.  
- After a recent price spike (sentiment > 0.27), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast decline in next 3-5 days to prevent overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model often underestimates downward trend — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.  
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days.  
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often ignores sentiment — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to align with sentiment-driven correction.
